## Status update: the usage-log half is fixed and landing (Gerrit 1435)

aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86 fixed the **usage-log** channel: `record()` no longer discards the seven
run-shape keys `failure_usage()` already computed, both the success and failure paths write them,
gate runs record with no env var set, and `python -m rebar.llm.usage_log summarize` now RENDERS
the loop-vs-breadth discriminator rather than merely storing it.

**This ticket is still entirely open** — it covers the SIDECAR channel, which is untouched:

1. `failure.py:82-96` `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` still admits `request_limit`/`tool_calls_limit` and
   neither `requests` nor `tool_calls`.
2. Five of six `emit_gate_error` sites still pass no diagnostic at all.
3. The completion verdict sidecar still carries no counts and no duration, while the plan-review
   sidecar already carries `requests` + a `metrics` block — the two gates remain asymmetric, and
   the completion gate (the one whose budget was raised five times) is the blind one.

**A concrete demonstration of why the sidecar half still matters.** With only the usage-log fix
in place, this question was answerable locally but NOT from the store — I had to read a
per-checkout `.rebar/usage.jsonl`:

    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier  185.6s  requests=0  sonnet-4-6  FAILED   (x4 runs)
    overlap-judge                      312-381s requests=3 sonnet-4-6  FAILED   (x5)
    64 ok / 9 failed = 12.3% call failure rate across three plan-review runs

That is exactly the shape of evidence rebar ticket 895c needs, and it is invisible to
`rebar audit show` and to every other agent, because it never reaches the ticket store. Closing
this ticket is what makes it shared rather than local.

# The SIDECAR channel records gate-run limits but not gate-run consumption

Discovered by the Step-7 sibling sweep while fixing [rebar:aec1-76e7-bb95-4c86]. `aec1` fixed the
**usage-log** channel (`.rebar/usage.jsonl`). The **sidecar** channel — the one an operator reaches
with `rebar audit show <ticket>`, and the one that lives in the store — still has the same defect in
three places.

## 1. The sanitization allowlist admits the ceiling and drops the measurement

`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:82-96` — `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` contains `request_limit` and
`tool_calls_limit` but **not** `requests` or `tool_calls`. So a gate error durably records *what the
limit was* and never *what was consumed*, which is precisely the half that makes the record
actionable. Identical construct to aec1's root cause: a fixed allowlist that admits the ceiling and
discards the measurement.

Both candidate fields are plain integers carrying no prompt, response or argument content, so this
is safe on the privacy contract — but `_ALLOWED_FIELDS` is a **sanitization boundary**, and widening
it is a privacy decision that deserves its own review rather than riding in on a telemetry fix.
That is why aec1 filed this instead of folding it in.

## 2. Five of six `emit_gate_error` call sites pass no diagnostic at all

`workflow/gate_dispatch.py:122, 180, 351, 467, 518` are all `cause=`-only. Only
`workflow/completion_recovery.py:388-395` passes a `diagnostic=`, and that is the completion
**bounded-recovery** arm alone (it seeds and allowlists `requests`/`tool_calls`/`tool_calls_limit`
at `:255-267`, which is why that one arm works). A plan-review gate error, or a completion
*preflight* gate error, therefore persists no counters whatsoever.

## 3. The completion verdict sidecar carries no run metadata at all

`completion_sidecar.py:271-306` — the payload is verdict/criteria/findings/remediation/runner/model/
`verified_at_sha`/`trace_id`/`material_fingerprint`/`certifiable`. No requests, no tool calls, no
duration. By contrast the plan-review sidecar already carries per-call `requests`
(`plan_review/sizing.py:292-310`) and a `metrics` block with `det_ms`/`llm_ms`/`total_ms`/
`llm_calls` (`workflow/plan_review_recovery.py:151-177`) — so the two gates are **asymmetric**, and
the completion gate (the one whose step budget was raised five times) is the blind one.

## Why this matters after aec1

aec1 makes the numbers exist on disk in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`, which is per-checkout and not shared.
The sidecar channel is the one that rides the ticket store and is therefore visible to every agent
and every later reader. Until this is closed, "how much did this ticket's gates cost" is answerable
locally but still not answerable **from the store** — the exact phrasing of the original complaint.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `requests` and `tool_calls` are admitted by `failure.py:_ALLOWED_FIELDS`, with the privacy
      rationale recorded next to them (integers only, no content)
- [ ] every `emit_gate_error` call site passes a diagnostic carrying the consumed counters, or the
      ticket records per-site why a given site legitimately has none
- [ ] the completion verdict sidecar carries requests/tool_calls/duration, reaching parity with the
      plan-review sidecar's existing `metrics` block
- [ ] a test proves the counters survive to the SIDECAR for a FAILING gate run, not only a passing
      one (the axis aec1 established must vary here too)
- [ ] `rebar audit show <ticket>` surfaces them
